Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring a finding of necessity for significant legislative rules by state agencies.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a finding of necessity for administrative rules;and adding new sections to chapter 34.05 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 34.05 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Before proposing a new rule or amending an existing rule that meetsthe definition of a significant legislative rule under RCW 34.05.328,a state agency shall adopt a finding of necessity demonstrating thatthe new or amended rule is necessary to implement a new legislative orfederal directive, or is required to fully implement the intent of anexisting state or federal law. The process includes the followingsteps: (1) The state agency shall identify the legislation or federal lawthat enables or directs the agency to adopt or to amend the applicablerule. (2) The state agency shall analyze and clearly define how and whythe proposed new or amended rule is required to achieve the intent ofthe enabling legislation. The state agency shall propose conclusions p. 1 HB 2616of law stating the authority of the agency to adopt or amend theapplicable rule. (3) The state agency shall propose findings of fact based upon ananalysis of the best available science or best available information.The findings must support a conclusion that the new or amended rulerequirements are supported by science or reputable information. (4) The state agency shall propose findings of fact thatdemonstrate that the proposed new or amended rule is the leastburdensome and most costeffective alternative to effectuate theenabling legislation or federal law. The agency shall provide a costbenefit analysis report. (5) The state agency shall file a notice of intent to adopt afinding of necessity with the code reviser for publication in the stateregister, establish a public comment period of thirty to sixty daysafter publication, and conduct at least four public hearings around thestate, equally divided as to east and west, to take public testimonyregarding the proposed conclusions of law, findings of fact, the agencydirector's proposed agency action, and the adoption of the finding ofnecessity. (6) Adoption of a finding of necessity and supporting conclusionsof law and findings of fact are required before filing the notice ofintent to adopt or amend a rule with the office of the code reviserunder RCW 34.05.320. (7) The action of adopting a finding of necessity may be appealedto the superior court of Thurston county or of the county of residenceof the appellant.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 34.05 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Agencies shall file proposed findings of necessity under section 1of this act by June 1st of each year. The final findings of necessitymust be filed by September 15th of each year.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 34.05 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A finding by a superior court that the state agency failed tocomply with the process for adoption of a finding of necessity under HB 2616 p. 2 section 1 of this act renders a finding of necessity and a significantlegislative rule adopted under it null and void.
